questions.q: In the capstone trigger, which phase defaults a blank CloseDate, and why doesn't it need an explicit update statement?
options: The before phase; before triggers can set fields directly on Trigger.new and the platform saves them automatically
The after phase; after triggers never need DML
The after phase; the recursion guard saves it instead
Neither phase — CloseDate is defaulted by a validation rule, not Apex
questions.explain: beforeSave() runs in the before phase and sets opp.CloseDate directly on the record in Trigger.new, which the platform persists without a separate DML call.

questions.q: Why does afterUpdate() collect AccountIds into a Set before querying, rather than querying inside the loop over newOpps?
options: Sets are required syntactically by SOQL
To bulkify: one query with WHERE Id IN handles the whole batch, instead of one query per Opportunity
Because Trigger.new cannot be looped over more than once
To avoid using a Map afterward
questions.explain: Collecting unique AccountIds first and querying once with IN keeps the handler at one SOQL query regardless of how many Opportunities are in the batch — the bulkification pattern from Lesson 23.

questions.q: What does the static accountsAlreadyMarkedHot Set prevent?
options: It prevents the before phase from running more than once
It prevents CloseDate from ever being blank
It prevents the handler from re-querying or re-updating an Account it has already marked Hot within the same transaction
It prevents Opportunities from being deleted
questions.explain: This is the recursion/re-processing guard from Lesson 24, implemented as a per-record Set<Id> rather than a single blunt boolean.

questions.q: In the lab's second scenario — updating an already-Closed-Won Opportunity's Amount field — why does the Account NOT get re-updated?
options: Because the trigger is deactivated after the first run
Because justWon evaluates false (StageName was already Closed Won before this update), so that Opportunity's AccountId is never added to accountIdsToHeat
Because Amount changes always bypass triggers
Because the Account was deleted in the first update
questions.explain: justWon only becomes true on the transition into Closed Won; since oldOpp.StageName is already Closed Won, the condition is false and that Account is correctly skipped.

questions.q: Why is OpportunityTrigger written as a single trigger that delegates to OpportunityTriggerHandler, instead of as separate before and after triggers?
options: Separate triggers on the same object run in a guaranteed, predictable order, so it doesn't matter
Apex does not allow more than one trigger event per trigger
Handler classes can only be called from a single combined trigger
One trigger per object keeps execution order explicit in the handler's code rather than left to the platform, per Lesson 22's best practice
questions.explain: Consolidating to one trigger per object and routing to a handler is exactly the practice from Lesson 22 — it keeps ordering and logic explicit and testable instead of relying on unguaranteed multi-trigger ordering.
